title: Recent Progress for Single-Molecule Magnets Based on Rare Earth Elements
claim: Zero-field quantum tunneling in TbPc2 produces butterfly hysteresis with very small low-temperature remanence and coercivity, limiting its use in high-density memory.
explanation: The review attributes the butterfly loop and weak remanence/coercivity of TbPc2 at low temperature to complex near-zero-field relaxation and magnetization quantum tunneling, and says this seriously hinders memory-device applications. Exchange coupling to substrates is mentioned as a related issue.
scope: TbPc2 and closely related double-decker Tb phthalocyanine SMMs.
conditions: Low temperature and near-zero magnetic field.
caveats: The statement is specific to TbPc2 behavior as reviewed; it is not a claim that all Tb SMMs lack remanence.
